habitat: Flocks in tall grass near forest fringes and thick bush, and in montane regions usually near wooded streams.
summary: A common endemic resident. Both sexes have a yellow belly and vent, a whitish breast, dark green upper parts and a crimson rump and upper tail coverts. The male has a black face. The usual call is a soft swee-swee. Newman says its range does not overlap Yellow-bellied Waxbill. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged. No openly licensed Kruger photograph was found.

similar.note: Common Waxbill has a red mask and red bill. Swee Waxbill has a yellow belly, a dark green back and a red rump, and the male has a black face.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^6=64 mature individuals (non-breeding visitor); paper interval half–double → 32–128.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

calls.description: A soft swee-swee. No grade A recording was in the catalogue set. Grade B call from the Drakensberg above Monk’s Cowl. The filename says the file was edited. It was not cleaned again.
